facts.fact: The article (Zahag, University of Blida 2) states that the National Automated Civil Status Register, established by ordinance 70-20 as amended by law 14-08 of 9 August 2014, is under the supervision of the Ministry of the Interior and connects all municipalities, their administrative annexes and consular offices abroad; it dates the statement no later than the law, so the published date is used.

The article states that the e-municipality programme, of which it names the National Automated Civil Status Register as a major initiative, is part of the national e-Algeria strategy, which it gives as running 2008-2028; no date is given for the statement, so the published date is used.

The article states that the register holds birth, marriage and death acts with their amendments, corrections and registrations, citing article 25 bis 1, and that data-entry errors are corrected centrally; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The article says the register connects all municipalities, their annexes and consular offices, but gives no count or share of offices entering births or deaths digitally, and finds that paper documentation persists alongside the digital services; no date is given, so the published date is used.

note: The article describes what the register holds and issues; it does not say that a commune enters a birth or death digitally at declaration, so no 'made' fact is taken. Its figure that about 82% of municipalities lack a working website concerns websites, not registration.
